source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Flexential Raleigh sits in Morrisville with 4.31 MW of published IT capacity across roughly 100,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 4.31 MW supports approximately 108 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a common colocation density for general enterprise workloads, the same power supports roughly 431 racks. The arithmetic is an assumption about density, not an operator claim. The campus is a mid-sized facility by absolute numbers, and the space-to-power ratio suggests it was not designed around the extreme rack densities that GPU clusters require today.

The six certifications tell a specific story about intended workload. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 qualify the campus for financial and operational audit trails. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data. HITRUST qualifies it for healthcare information. ISO 27001 and SSAE 18 address information security management and reporting standards. Taken together, the certifications point toward regulated enterprise workloads, not toward the permissive, high-density AI training environments that prioritize raw power over compliance posture.

Among the 19 facilities this site has mapped in North Carolina, only 5 publish a megawatt figure. Those five sum to 51.47 MW, and Flexential Raleigh at 4.31 MW ranks second among them. That rank reflects the limits of published data, not a complete picture of North Carolina capacity. Most mapped facilities in the state publish no figure at all. For a reader evaluating AI scaling potential, the campus is notable for its compliance depth and its relative standing in a state where published capacity data is sparse, but 4.31 MW of IT load is a fraction of what a serious AI training deployment consumes.
